title: Hegseth vows to keep fighting from Pentagon, defends Iran war
summary: WASHINGTON — US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a video message on Thursday vowing to fight efforts in Congress to impeach him and defending the Iran war as “courageous and historic” after voters punished Republicans over it in this week’s midterm elections. Hegseth's remarks, posted on social media, came as taunts from his foes in Congress intensified and President Donald Trump swatted away questions about whether he might fire Hegseth. Trump has commended his Pentagon chief. The top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, asked in a post: "Why is Pete Hegseth still around?" title: Wisconsin reports infant death linked to measles outbreak
summary: The Wisconsin Department of Health Services said on Thursday that an infant had died in connection with the ongoing measles outbreak in the state. The coroner listed measles as the immediate cause of death, the department said, declining to release further details to protect the family's privacy. The death comes as the United States faces its highest number of measles cases in decades, fueled by outbreaks in several states and declining childhood vaccination rates in some communities. Wisconsin had reported 431 cases across 13 counties as of November 3, with nine people hospitalized for severe symptoms. title: Seventeen's Joshua brings bold elegance to Vogue Korea digital covers
summary: Seventeen member Joshua is putting his growing influence in fashion and beauty on display, appearing in three digital covers for Vogue Korea in collaboration with luxury brand Tom Ford Beauty. Vogue Korea released the three covers on its official social media accounts on Thursday, showcasing Joshua in a photo shoot themed “Bold Ambition.” The images pair his sophisticated appeal with daring styling, highlighting a more mature and refined look in collaboration with Tom Ford Beauty, for which he serves as an ambassador. In an accompanying interview, Joshua discussed his ambitions to continue developing as an artist and explore new creative opportunities. title: Rohingya Muslim refugees who fled persecution in Myanmar face new challenges in Malaysia
summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia — Nur Sadek was once on track to become an Islamic scholar. His mother dreamed of raising a son who would serve as a faith leader in their western Myanmar village. Sadek’s family belongs to the Rohingya ethnic minority. The predominantly Muslim group shares an area in Myanmar's Rakhine State with Buddhists and a smaller Hindu population. Ethnic and religious divisions have long shaped the region’s history. He fled alongside loved ones in 2017 after soldiers opened fire on his community and bullets struck the tin roof of his home. He ran with nothing but the clothes on his back and never returned. title: Russia and Ukraine exchange airstrikes as US envoy describes renewed security talks as productive
summary: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia and Ukraine exchanged airstrikes overnight as the second day of talks on Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction and security guarantees once the fighting ends wrapped up in Brussels on Thursday. The latest Russian aerial barrage underscored the scale of the rebuilding task, as did the continuing search for people missing beneath the rubble after a deadly airstrike in southern Ukraine on Monday. Ukraine launched hundreds of drones at Russian targets. Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces shot down nearly 500 drones overnight. title: N. Korea says Japan's push to raise defense spending will only burden its people
summary: North Korea on Friday criticized Japan's push to increase defense spending, saying it will darken prospects of Japan's economic recovery and impose "heavy hardships" on its people. In an article carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), a researcher at the Institute for Japan Studies under the North's foreign ministry, issued the criticism, following reports that Tokyo is considering nearly doubling its defense expenditures over the next five years. The North has long responded sensitively to Japan's military reinforcement plans, arguing they could worsen a regional arms race, heighten military tensions and bring back memories of Tokyo's past militarism. title: Finance minister vows timely actions to ease stock market volatility
summary: The country's finance minister said Friday that the financial authorities will map out measures to help the local stock market be less volatile amid the ongoing tech rout. In an economy-related meeting, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said the U.S. midterm elections are an important watershed for the global economy, saying that overnight falls on Wall Street in the face of tighter regulations on AI-related sectors would deliver a blow to the global market. Lee said the Korean economy's fundamentals are more solid than ever before and vowed to respond to external uncertainties. Shortly after the opening bell, trading of the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for 20 minutes, as the benchmark index plunged by more than 8 percent amid tech sell-offs.

title: [COVER STORY] Black Friday: KOSPI sinks 6%, extending slide on US AI regulation fears
summary: KOSPI plunged more than 6 percent Friday, barely holding above the 5,000 mark, as fears of tighter U.S. regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers sparked panic selling in chip stocks. The benchmark finished at 5,059.69, shedding 324.11 points, or 6.02 percent, following a 5.28 percent decline the previous day. After opening 2.24 percent lower at 5,263.26, the index quickly lost more ground, falling over 8 percent and slipping below 5,000 for the first time since Feb. 6. The plunge triggered a first-stage circuit breaker at around 9:03 a.m., suspending trading for 20 minutes. Renewed selling after trading resumed prompted a sell-side sidecar at around 9:34 a.m., temporarily suspending the execution of program sell orders. title: Trading of KOSPI stocks suspended amid tech sell-off
summary: Korea's bourse operator on Friday activated a circuit breaker for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) on an extended sell-off in tech shares. Trading of KOSPI-listed shares was halted for 20 minutes from 9:03, as the index plunged more than 8 percent from the previous session's close. The benchmark index came under heavy selling pressure following a tech rout on Wall Street, triggered by concerns that Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterms could slow down the pace of the build out of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. It marked the tenth time this year that the KRX has activated a circuit breaker.

title: Seoul stocks sharply down late Friday morning on AI rout
summary: Seoul stocks were trading sharply lower late Friday morning on concerns that the Democratic Party of Korea's sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm election could slow the construction of data centers. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) was down 240.41 points, or 4.47 percent, to 5,143.39 as of 11:20 a.m. Shortly after the opening bell, the Korea Exchange (KRX) had suspended trading of the KOSPI stocks for 20 minutes as the index tumbled by more than 8 percent. Overnight, major stock indexes on Wall Street tumbled following the midterm election results, as investors sold off market top-caps in artificial intelligence (AI) and data centers. title: Deputy FM meets British lawmakers for talks on N. Korea, Ukraine
summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Chung Eui-hae has met with a delegation of British lawmakers to discuss bilateral relations and major regional issues, including the Korean Peninsula and the war in Ukraine, Seoul's foreign ministry said Friday. Chung met with a six-member delegation, led by Alicia Kearns of the House of Commons and including two members of the House of Lords, Godfrey Bewicke-Copley and Tessa Blackstone, in Seoul the previous day, according to the ministry. The two sides exchanged views on regional developments, including the Korean Peninsula, Ukraine and the Strait of Hormuz, and agreed to strengthen coordination at international forums, such as the Group of 20 (G20). title: S. Korea agrees to support East Timor's economic, social development
summary: South Korea and East Timor agreed Friday to strengthen development cooperation to facilitate Seoul's assistance to the Southeast Asian country's economic and social development while working closely together in intellectual property and climate change responses. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and East Timorese President Jose Ramos-Horta reached the agreements during their summit at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, marking the first official visit by an East Timorese leader to South Korea since they established diplomatic relations in 2002. The summit came ahead of the 25th anniversary next year of the two countries' diplomatic relations. title: N. Korea lambasts money-laundering watchdog over renewed 'high-risk' label
summary: North Korea on Friday denounced the intergovernmental anti-money laundering body for keeping Pyongyang on its blacklist, claiming the agency serves the United States' hostile policy toward it. At a meeting in Paris in late October, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) decided to keep the North on its list of a "high-risk jurisdiction subject to a call for action." The designation applies to countries with serious failings in preventing money laundering, terrorist financing and weapons proliferation. "The Foreign Ministry of the DPRK expresses strong displeasure" over the FATF's practice of "encroaching upon the dignity, rights and interests of a sovereign state," a ministry spokesperson said in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). title: Koreans in US welcome Democratic wins, but doubts linger over what comes next
summary: SEATTLE — The Democrats' sweeping victories in Tuesday's (local time) U.S. midterm elections brought relief to many Koreans frustrated with President Donald Trump, but that relief did not necessarily translate into support for the Democratic Party. "Democrats didn't win. Republicans lost." That was how Bo Young Lee, a Korean American business executive, summed up the election results. "Ultimately, the results on Tuesday were a byproduct of citizens' frustration with the Trump administration, rising costs, and the attacks on democracy," Lee, an international speaker specializing in artificial intelligence ethics and corporate diversity, told The Korea Times. title: Melania Trump calls for lasting peace after brokering local Russia-Ukraine ceasefire
summary: WASHINGTON — U.S. first lady Melania Trump on Thursday called for continued cooperation between Russia and Ukraine toward lasting peace after helping broker a local ceasefire in southern Ukraine last month. Speaking at the White House with representatives from both countries in attendance, the first lady highlighted the humanitarian achievements of the recent ceasefire in Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region. The ceasefire, which began Oct. 27, lasted six days, according to foreign media reports. "Every significant transformation begins with a small spark," she said. "Ignite hope, foster cooperation and brighten a path toward lasting peace." title: 90 mil. displaced people at risk from climate threats, UN refugee agency says
summary: GENEVA — Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people are living in countries increasingly exposed to climate-related droughts, floods and extreme heat, the UN refugee agency said on Friday, warning ahead of the COP31 climate summit that more funding is needed to help vulnerable communities adapt. Nearly three-quarters of the world's forcibly displaced people are living in countries such as Afghanistan and Bangladesh that are exposed to severe climate-related risks, according to the report by the agency, known as UNHCR, published ahead of the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey. The findings show the overlap between conflict, displacement and climate change, the report said. title: More than dozen flights in Europe receive bomb threats that an official calls 'malicious' hoaxes
summary: MILAN — Bomb threats targeted more than a dozen flights in Europe on Thursday, leading to a slew of emergency landings and military escorts in some cases, authorities said. No hazardous or suspicious materials have been found in what a British official called “malicious" hoaxes. Several similar threats targeted planes earlier this week, prompting searches and diversions, with at least 25 flights targeted, officials said. Europe has experienced a slew of other disruptions recently, such as attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems, drone incursions and mysterious triggers to alert apps. While fake bomb threats are relatively common, it is unusual to see so many in a single day. title: S. Korea should deepen work with US, Japan on sanctions against NK after Binance theft: expert
summary: WASHINGTON — A U.S. cryptocurrency expert on Thursday called for South Korea to strengthen cooperation with the United States and Japan through unilateral and multilateral sanctions to counter North Korean cryptocurrency theft, including a recent major incident involving Binance. "South Korea should also deepen joint work with the United States and Japan to put additional pressure on North Korea," said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at U.S. blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, in a written response to Yonhap News Agency's inquiry on South Korea's response to last week's major theft at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. title: [FRIENDS OF KOREA] An American teenager in Seoul in 1967
summary: I was 13 when our family of 10 (mom, dad and eight kids ranging in age from 1 to 15) arrived at Kimpo Airport in August 1966. We arrived a bit prior to the first volunteers of the Peace Corps K-1, because our school started in early September. The older kids attended Seoul Foreign School (SFS) in Yeonhui-dong, behind Yonsei University. In fact, the founders of our school were some of the same missionaries who founded Yonsei, such as the Underwoods, the Allens and the Avisons. Today, there is a statue to Horace Grant Underwood in front of one of the Yonsei buildings. summary: As I trudged across Sinchon Rotary and up the steep walkway to Severance Hospital, I kept repeating to myself a phrase from a childhood story about a train engine: “I think I can, I think I can.” It was a bitter cold winter morning in 1969. Today was the day that I was to come to the hospital and show the doctors in the ear, nose and throat section of the hospital that I could, indeed, get a deaf child to speak. Only days earlier, I had arrived in Korea to volunteer for the Peace Corps at age 23. Once it got around that I had training as a speech therapist for the deaf, Peace Corps Korea Director Kevin O'Donnell urged me to pursue it. At the time, Korea had no speech pathology center. title: [FRIENDS OF KOREA] Two Peace Corps Volunteers' brush with cinematic fame in 1960s Myeong-dong
summary: One evening in Seoul, having nothing better to do, I decided to go out on the town in Myeong-dong with my friend Ron Rezac, a fellow Peace Corps Volunteer. Back in the 1960s, Myeong-dong was a trendy spot for Korean youth, filled with bars, cafes and music venues. After a few hours and a few beers (maybe more than a few), I let it be known that I, strangely, wanted to cap off the evening with some tea. title: Children bear cost of adoption delays, advocate says
summary: Children awaiting adoption in Korea are losing precious time to form bonds with permanent families as lengthy reviews and unclear screening standards delay placements, the head of an adoptive families’ advocacy group said. In an interview with The Korea Times after a press conference Tuesday outside the Board of Audit and Inspection in central Seoul, Oh Chang-hwa, head of the National Adoptive Family Federation, called for faster adoption matching and transparent assessment standards. “Children are there and parents are there. But they cannot meet,” he said. title: Namdaemun Market emerges as new shopping destination for foreign tourists
summary: Namdaemun Market in Seoul is attracting growing numbers of foreign tourists, as visitors increasingly venture beyond familiar shopping destinations such as Myeong-dong and Gangnam to explore traditional markets, data showed Thursday. According to data accumulated by Shinhan Card, card sales at tourism-related businesses at Namdaemun Market totaled 109.18 billion won ($81.4 million) in the January-September period, up 7.5 percent from a year earlier. Spending by foreign cardholders jumped 65.6 percent to 15.76 billion won, from 9.51 billion won a year earlier. Spending by domestic cardholders, by contrast, rose just 1.5 percent, from 92.01 billion won to 93.42 billion won. title: Documentary spotlights Peace Corps Volunteer's role in Gwangju Uprising
summary: The 1980 Gwangju Uprising produced a great many memorable photos, not least of which was one of a young man with blonde hair helping carry a man on a stretcher through the streets. The identity of this foreigner remained a mystery for decades, but as U.S. Peace Corps Volunteers (PCV) who were there began publishing their memoirs, his identity and role in the uprising gradually came into focus. The person in the photo was a PCV named Tim Warnberg, who had arrived in Korea in 1978 to work as a health volunteer at Gwangju Christian Hospital. Those who knew him before his arrival in Korea remember him as someone whose character and concern for others help explain his actions in 1980. title: Remembering Peace Corps' 15 years in Korea
summary: It may come as a shock to many these days that the Peace Corps once had a mission in Korea. The U.S. volunteer agency sent more than 2,000 young volunteers to Korea between 1966 and 1981 in 51 waves, from K-1 to K-51. The country they arrived in was very different from the advanced nation Korea has grown to become. Coming out of the 1910-45 Japanese occupation and 1950-53 Korean War, Korea was for decades one of the poorest nations in the world. In the mid-1960s, when Peace Corps Volunteers (PCVs) began arriving, Korea's hills were barren, and the gutters were filled with human waste. title: Foreign residents' first hurdle is housing. Enkostay says it can clear it.
summary: For many foreign residents, the first few weeks in Seoul can feel almost effortless. The subway works. Convenience stores are everywhere, and there is always another café, restaurant or corner of the city to discover. Then the paperwork begins. An appointment for a residence card. A landlord asking for a deposit that can run into the tens of millions of won. Almost overnight, the experience shifts from exploring Korea to deciphering it. For years, newcomers have leaned on Facebook groups for answers, and learned to sift through thousands of unverified listings and contradictory advice. The Nasdaq 100 index was set for market-value declines exceeding $2 trillion on investor fears that the Democratic Party's sweeping midterm victorycould stall AI infrastructure expansion and force a chaotic reckoning for smaller firms whose capacity to raise funds has already been limited by higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions. title: 박윤주 제1차관, 벨기에 외교부 사무차관 면담(11.6.)
summary: 박윤주 외교부 제1차관은 방한 중인 「테오도라 겐치스 (Theodora Gentzis)」 벨기에 외교부 사무차관과 11월 6일 면담을 갖고, 지난 6월 이재명 대통령의 벨기에 방문 계기 개최된 양국간 정상회담 후속조치 현황을 점검하고, 양국간 실질협력 강화 방안 및 주요 지역·글로벌 정세에 대해서도 의견을 교환하였다. 박 차관은 올해 우리 정상의 벨기에 양자 방문을 통해 경제·통상, 과학기술, 교육 등 다양한 분야에서 양국 협력을 한층 발전시킬 새로운 동력이 마련된 점을 평가하였다. 겐치스 사무차관은 수교 125주년을 맞는 뜻깊은 해에 이 대통령의 벨기에 방문이 이루어진 점이 매우 의미있다고 하고, 이를 기반으로 양국간 실질협력이 더욱 확대되기를 희망한다고 하였다. 양 차관은 중소기업 및 스타트업 발전 협력, 겐트대학교 송도캠퍼스 내 대학원 과정 신설 추진 등 정상간 합의사항들이 양국 국민과 기업이 체감할 수 있는 실질적인 성과로 이어지도록 후속조치를 충실히 이행해 나가기로 하였다. 또한, 양국 간 교역과 투자가 더욱 확대될 수 있도록 기업 활동에 우호적 여건을 조성하기 위해 함께 노력해 나가기로 하였다. 양 차관은 또한 실질협력 지속 확대를 위해 고위급 협의 채널을 활성화할 필요가 있다는 데 공감하고, 조속한 시일 내 차관보급 한-벨기에 정책협의회 개최를 추진해 나가기로 하였다. ※ 한-벨 정책협의회(차관보급)은 1981-99년간 총 10차례 개최되었으며, 1999년 제10차 회의(서울) 이후 미개최 겐치스 사무차관은 다자주의 및 규범 기반 국제질서가 도전에 직면한 상황에서 유사입장국이자 주요파트너인 한국과

title: 한·미·일 해외재난대응협력 협의체 회의 개최
summary: 2026.11.5.(목) 한·미·일 해외재난대응협력 협의체 회의가 각국 외교부, 국방부 등 관계기관이 참석*한 가운데 화상으로 개최되었다. 참석자들은 대규모 해외재난이 발생하여 인도적 위기가 촉발되었을 때, 이를 해소 및 완화할 수 있는 3국 협력 방안을 논의했다. * 우리측은 외교부 다자협력인도지원과장을 수석대표로 외교부, 한국국제협력단(KOICA), 국방부 담당자 참석 ※ 한·미·일 해외재난대응협력 협의체는 해외에서 대규모 재난 발생 시 긴급구호대 파견, 인도적 지원 등에서 한·미·일 협력 방안을 모색하기 위해 2026년 신설되었으며, 1차 회의(7.22, 화상), 2차 회의(9.3, 도쿄) 등 개최 해외재난 대응 분야에서 선진 제도와 높은 역량을 갖춘 한·미·일의 협력 강화를 통해 인도적 지원 효과성을 제고할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다. 우리부는 앞으로도 한·미·일 해외재난대응협력 협의체에 적극 참여하면서 논의를 주도해 나갈 계획이다. 끝.

title: 한일 초임 외교관 교류사업 실시
summary: 외교부는 11.9.-11.20. 2주간 한일 초임 외교관 교류사업의 일환으로 초임 외교관 1인을 일본 외무성에 파견한다. 동 사업은 1998년 10월 김대중 대통령-오부치 총리간 합의한 ｢21세기 새로운 한‧일 파트너십 공동선언｣ 후속조치의 일환으로 시작되었으며, 2025년 한일 국교정상화 60주년 계기 양국 외교당국 간 합의에 따라 재개되었다. 이번 파견은 금년 4월 일본측 초임 외교관 1인 접수에 이어 추진되는 것으로, 양국 실무 외교관들의 상호 이해와 신뢰 증진, 외교당국 간 교류 활성화 등을 통해 한‧일 간 우호협력 관계 발전에 기여할 것으로 기대된다. 끝.

title: 외교부, 제8차 여성과 함께하는 평화 국제회의 개최 예정(11.11.)
summary: 외교부는 11.11.(수) 더그랜드롯데 서울에서 ‘지속가능한 평화를 위한 여성·평화·안보(WPS) 혁신’을 주제로 제8차 「여성과 함께하는 평화(Action with Women and Peace, AWP) 국제회의」를 개최한다. 지난해 유엔 안보리 결의 1325호 채택 25주년 계기 성과 점검을 토대로, 올해 회의는 여성·평화·안보(WPS) 의제를 한 단계 더 발전시킬 새로운 방안을 찾는 데 무게를 둔다. ※ 여성·평화·안보(WPS: Women, Peace and Security) : 분쟁 상황에서 여성을 보호하고, 평화 협상·구축 과정에서 여성의 참여와 역할을 확대하자는 국제 의제로, 2000년 유엔 안보리 결의 1325 채택을 계기로 본격화 이번 국제회의는 장욱진 외교부 글로벌다자외교조정관의 개회사에 이어, ▴크리스틴 아랍(Christine Arab) UN Women 아태지역사무소장, ▴아와 다보(Awa Dabo) 유엔 인권부최고대표, ▴자이나브 방구라(Zainab Bangura) 유엔 나이로비사무소장, ▴이레네 펠린(Irene Fellin) NATO 사무총장 WPS 특별대표 등 주요 국제기구 인사 및 WPS 분야 전문가들이 기조연설과 축사를 전한다. 패널세션 1에서는 ‘지속가능한 평화를 위한 생존자의 기여’를 주제로 아시아·태평양 지역의 평화에 기여하는 여성의 역할을 조명하고, 새로운 WPS의 해법을 모색한다. ‘AI를 통한 WPS 혁신’ 제하의 패널세션 2에서는 WPS 영역에서 AI가 제공하는 기회와 위험을 균형 있게 다루며, 이어지는 청년 세션에서는 ‘미래를 위한 WPS 혁신을 선도하는 청년’을 주제

title: 한-보스니아·헤르체고비나  경제협력협정 발효
summary: 「대한민국과 보스니아·헤르체고비나 간의 경제협력에 관한 협정」이 11.6.(금) 발효한다. ※ 경제협력협정은 양국간 투자, 관광, 농업, 환경 등 다양한 분야에서의 협력을 포괄적으로 아우르는 양국간 기초적인 경제협력의 틀을 다루는 조약 보스니아·헤르체고비나는 남동유럽에 위치한 전력 순수출국으로 최근 신재생 에너지 중심의 에너지 전환을 추진하고 있으며, 풍부한 산림 자원을 바탕으로 목재 가공 및 가구 산업을 적극적으로 육성해가고 있다. 금번 협정의 발효를 통해 보스니아·헤르체고비나와의 경제협력이 공고해지고, 우리 기업의 발칸 지역진출을 위한 제도적 기반이 마련된 것으로 평가된다. 또한, 동 협정에 따라 양국은 필요시 경제 및 기술전문가 회의를 설치하여 협정 이행 상황을 점검하고 경제협력 강화 방안을 논의할 수 있게 되어, 양국간 실질 협력이 한층 강화될 것으로 기대된다. 양국간 연간 교역규모는 4,159만 달러(2025년)로, 한국은 주로 철강, 전자기기, 자동차 부품 등을 수출 중이며, 보스니아·헤르체고비나는 납광, 의류 등을 주로 수출하고 있다. ※ 양국 교역 현황 : 4,159만 달러(수출: 1,042만 달러, 수입 : 3,117만 달러) (2025, 한국무역협회) 이번 한-보스니아·헤르체고비나 경제협력협정으로 우리나라는 102개의 경제협력협정을 발효하게 되었으며, 정부는 앞으로도 우리 경제외교 네트워크 확장과 우리 기업의 글로벌 시장 진출을 위해 경제협력협정을 지속 체결해 나갈 계획이다. 끝.
